boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Colorado Boulder, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical, under-21-safe sequence for learning campus, meeting people, and stepping into Boulder’s public spaces.

cards.title: Start by pinning your bearings
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main Campus
cards.notes: Open the map before heading out. Search your residence hall, the UMC and Norlin, then use its walking directions to make a simple first loop.
cards.short_summary: A map-first walk turns unfamiliar campus landmarks into repeatable routes.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder says its interactive map supports searchable locations, campus layers, and walking, driving, and biking directions.
cards.source_title: How to Use the CU Boulder Interactive Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Use the public web map; it includes accessibility, transportation, dining, and building-information layers.

cards.title: Make the UMC your first meetup point
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 1669 Euclid Ave.
cards.notes: Meet a classmate in the UMC, scan the events listing and locate its student services. Keep the building in mind as an easy indoor reset point.
cards.short_summary: The UMC combines student services, events, dining, and places to spend time.
cards.evidence_claim: The UMC identifies dining options, student services, involvement opportunities, NightRide, and The Connection as offerings in the building.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1669 Euclid Avenue, at Broadway and Euclid; construction is noted on the UMC home page for spring and summer 2026.

cards.title: Choose a study spot before classes speed up
cards.subtitle: Friday late afternoon · 1720 Pleasant St.
cards.notes: Walk all five floors, pick one seat you would return to, and save the library’s hours page. Reserve a group room later if you need one.
cards.short_summary: A first visit makes the campus’s largest library feel immediately usable.
cards.evidence_claim: Norlin Library is CU Boulder’s largest library and offers five floors, group-study-room reservations, research help, and multiple collections.
cards.access_notes: Hours may change; check the library’s current hours link before relying on a visit time.

cards.title: Take the long way across Norlin Quad
cards.subtitle: Friday near sunset · Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the quad as the connective walk between Old Main and Norlin. Pause to identify the routes you will use for classes rather than rushing through.
cards.short_summary: A historic central landscape makes a calm orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder states that Norlin Quadrangle, including original Old Main, is listed in the State and National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus walk; use the interactive campus map for current walking directions.

cards.title: Try a low-key game at The Connection
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · UMC Room 105
cards.notes: Bring a few new neighbors for bowling, billiards, or games. Check lane availability and the current schedule before you head over.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop that gives a new group something concrete to do.
cards.evidence_claim: The Connection is inside the UMC and offers bowling, billiards, snacks, and games; its official page lists current seasonal operating hours.
cards.source_title: The Connection: Location, Contact and Hours
cards.access_notes: Summer hours listed are daily 12–9 p.m. through Aug. 15; fall/spring hours list Thursday–Saturday until 11 p.m. Confirm availability before visiting.

cards.title: Locate Folsom Field on your campus loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Stadium Drive
cards.notes: Walk by the stadium and connect it to the nearby recreation and athletics area. Check the official calendar later for any event you want to attend.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus landmark helps anchor the east side of Main Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder’s visitor information identifies sporting and athletics events as campus activities, and the official campus map labels Folsom Field.
cards.access_notes: Viewing the exterior is a self-guided campus walk; event entry and ticketing depend on the specific event.

cards.title: Pause beside Varsity Lake
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · East edge of Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find Varsity Lake, then take a short outdoor break before continuing toward the recreation and stadium area.
cards.short_summary: A named campus water feature provides a clear waypoint on a self-guided walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The official CU Boulder campus map labels Varsity Lake on Main Campus near Folsom Field and recreation facilities.
cards.access_notes: Use the current interactive campus map for routing and any access updates.

cards.title: Walk the Pearl Street Mall without an agenda
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Downtown Boulder
cards.notes: Take a slow pass through the pedestrian mall, notice public art and storefronts, and pick one landmark to revisit with friends another weekend.
cards.short_summary: Downtown Boulder’s pedestrian center offers an easy off-campus orientation walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Boulder Partnership describes the Pearl Street Mall as a downtown gathering place with shopping, dining, services, and special events.
cards.access_notes: Individual storefront hours vary by season; the downtown FAQ directs visitors to check businesses individually.

cards.title: Look for art in the Boulder Alley Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Downtown Boulder
cards.notes: Turn the Pearl Street visit into a short art walk. Find several painted alley doors, take a photo, and keep moving through the public downtown district.
cards.short_summary: A continuing outdoor art program offers a specific visual scavenger-hunt stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Boulder Community Initiatives describes the Boulder Alley Gallery as an outdoor artist gallery that repurposes alley and back-of-building doors.
cards.access_notes: The program is in the downtown district; consult the organizer’s Alley Gallery map before setting out.

cards.title: Close with a daylight Chautauqua walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · 900 Baseline Rd.
cards.notes: Choose the Chautauqua Trail for a short out-and-back, bring water, and read the interpretive signs. Check trail status and conditions immediately before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A mapped, easy-to-medium trail gives a first weekend a careful outdoor finish.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Boulder lists Chautauqua Trail as a 1.2-mile out-and-back route through Chautauqua Meadow and advises visitors to pack extra water.
cards.access_notes: The trailhead is listed as open daily 5 a.m.–11 p.m.; the city lists no trailhead fee, but notes summer parking fees may apply.

warnings: The CU Museum of Natural History was excluded because its official FAQ says it is closed until fall 2026.
